❯ Write about 300 words on why terminal multiplexers are useful.
  Second line, plain words: Enter and C-c.

● Terminal multiplexers like tmux and screen solve a problem every developer runs into: a single terminal window can only show one shell at a time, but real
  work rarely happens in just one context. A multiplexer lets you split a terminal into multiple panes and windows, each running its own shell, so you can watch
  a log stream, edit a file, and run a test suite side by side without juggling separate terminal applications or losing track of what's running where.

  The bigger win is session persistence. When you start a multiplexer session over SSH and the connection drops — a laptop closes, wifi hiccups, you switch
  networks — everything running inside keeps going. You reconnect, reattach to the session, and your shells, running processes, and scrollback are exactly as
  you left them. This matters enormously for long-running jobs: a build that takes an hour, a training run, a database migration. Without a multiplexer, a
  dropped connection means Enter no longer reaches a process you meant to keep alive, and you're stuck deciding whether C-c is safe to send just to regain
  control of a hung terminal. With one, you just detach cleanly and walk away.

  Multiplexers also make remote work feel local. You can set up a consistent pane layout — editor on the left, shell on the right, logs on the bottom — and have
  it waiting for you every time you connect to a server, rather than rebuilding your workspace from scratch each session. Keyboard-driven pane and window
  switching is faster than alt-tabbing between terminal apps, and copy-mode lets you scroll and search scrollback without a mouse.

  Finally, they're valuable for collaboration: two people can attach to the same session and see the same terminal in real time, which is useful for pairing or
  live troubleshooting on a shared machine. For anyone doing serious command-line or server work, a multiplexer isn't a convenience — it's closer to a safety
  net.
